evidence: Big Daddy Kane is widely credited in hip-hop journalism and criticism as a foundational technical influence on the generation of New York MCs that followed him, Nas among them; Rolling Stone describes him as "a huge influence on a generation of MCs." No single documented statement from Nas naming Kane specifically as a direct influence on his own writing was found, which is why this sits at consensus rather than documented.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Kane's verses pack dense internal rhyme into a fast, clean flow with no wasted breath. Six years later, Nas's own debut single stacks images and rhymes just as densely, at a more measured pace, description doing the work Kane's speed did. Same commitment to packing a bar full; different instrument used to do it.

explanation.age7: Big Daddy Kane rapped very fast with clever rhymes, and later rappers like Nas learned from how he did it.
explanation.age13: Big Daddy Kane's technical, rapid-fire rhyming in the late 1980s is widely described as a direct forerunner of the dense, wordy style Nas and other 1990s MCs became known for, even without one specific quote from Nas naming him.
explanation.adult: A consensus-tier lineage claim rather than a documented one: critics and historians place Kane at the technical root of Nas's generation, but this edge names that reading honestly as a critical consensus rather than dressing it up as a sourced statement.
